questions.learningObjective: Identify a fusion fuel isotope
questions.stem: A transit planner asks which isotopes are commonly used in fusion reactors?
questions.explanation: Deuterium and tritium are the common fusion fuels. Uranium and plutonium are fission fuels, and helium-3 alone is not the standard pair.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.learningObjective: Compute the daughter element symbol
questions.stem: A transit planner decays thorium-232 by alpha; what element is the daughter?
questions.explanation: Alpha decay reduces atomic number by 2, so thorium (90) becomes radium (88). No change or an increase is wrong.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.learningObjective: Compute the daughter atomic number
questions.stem: A transit planner starts with strontium-90 (atomic number 38) and emits beta-minus; what is the daughter atomic number?
questions.explanation: Beta-minus decay increases atomic number by 1, so 38 plus 1 equals 39, which is yttrium. Mass number stays 90.
questions.hint: Add one to the atomic number.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.learningObjective: Compute elapsed time from remaining fraction
questions.stem: A transit planner has 1/32 remaining with half-life 2 h; how many hours elapsed?
questions.explanation: 1/32 is 1 over 2 to the 5th, five half-lives, so 5 times 2 hours equals 10 hours. Four half-lives would leave 1/16.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.learningObjective: Compute the decay constant from a table
questions.stem: A transit planner reads half-life 4 min from a table; what is lambda in per minute?
questions.explanation: Lambda equals ln2 over half-life, so 0.693 over 4 minutes is 0.1733 per minute. Using 1 over 4 would be wrong.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.learningObjective: Identify the mass number change in fission
questions.stem: A transit planner asks what is conserved in nuclear fission?

options.text: Mass number and atomic number (with neutron bookkeeping)

questions.explanation: Nucleon number and charge are conserved in fission, with neutrons balancing the books. Energy is released but not at the expense of conservation.
questions.hint: What must balance in a nuclear equation?

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.learningObjective: Summarize the beta-minus decay process
questions.stem: A transit planner summarizes beta-minus decay; which statement is correct?

options.text: A proton becomes a neutron, emitting a positron
A neutron becomes a proton, emitting an electron and antineutrino

questions.explanation: Beta-minus decay converts a neutron to a proton and emits an electron plus antineutrino, raising atomic number by 1. Mass number stays the same.
